output.scope_note: The paper reports Li-ion conductivity values (18.1 mS cm-1 at 25 °C and temperature series) for lithiated Ketjen Black measured in a solid-state Li/C/LPSCl/C/Li cell, so it reports at least one ionic conductivity of a solid Li-ion conductor, although the material is a carbon rather than a conventional solid electrolyte.

records.measurement_method: DC method on symmetric Li/C/LPSCl/C/Li cell
records.evidence_quote: Li-KB has Li ionic conductivity values of 18.1, 25.8, 41.1, 53.2 and 69.6 mS cm-1 at 25, 40, 60, 80 and 100 oC, respectively.
records.notes: Value at 25 °C taken from the text sentence listing values at 25–100 °C; the abstract gives the same 18.1 mS cm-1 at room temperature. Activation energy 0.17 eV is stated in the following sentence of the paper (Arrhenius fit for Li-KB). Conductivity is derived from DC ionic resistance of the carbon interlayer, not a conventional bulk electrolyte measurement; the material is a lithiated carbon black, so it is an unconventional case for a solid Li conductor. Other conductivities (Li-SP, Li-Gr) are given only as ratios, not as numbers, and are not recorded.
